title: Parameter Golf with AutoResearch — Vayum Arora, Zhengyao Jiang, Dixing Xu & Dhruv Srikanth, Weco AI
talk_summary: Weco AI describes an 'auto research' loop where an agent repeatedly edits a single source file, runs a fast, low-noise, scalar-metric eval, and keeps only improvements, using tree-based search over attempts. They report their agent Aiden placed as top contributor in OpenAI's Parameter Golf with 4% of community compute and 15% of merged records, and stress eval design, bounded eval time, observability, and human steerability.

takeaways.technique: Single-scalar fast low-noise eval as the optimization contract
takeaways.what_they_do: Every candidate change is scored by one cheap, fast, low-noise scalar metric printed to the terminal, which the agent parses to decide keep/discard; they explicitly warn agents reward-hack the eval so it must be hardened.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you want to have it output a single scalar metric. And you want the eval to be fast, you want it to be cheap, you want it to have low noise

takeaways.technique: Tree-based search over attempts with pruning
takeaways.what_they_do: Treats optimization as an experiment graph: root is baseline, each node is a code change with a score, branches that improve go deeper and bad ones are pruned, so ideas compound instead of restarting from scratch.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the search builds on what works. We're finding good candidates and pruning bad ones
takeaways.numbers: Aiden landed 7 leaderboard records, twice the next best human; 435 downstream PRs built on its work

takeaways.technique: Hard wall-clock bound on every eval run
takeaways.what_they_do: Caps each evaluation at 210s split into fixed phases (60s train, 60s test, 90s buffer for GPU spin-up), because loops stall, hardware fails, and bad agent code hangs the system.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you want to bound the the actual evaluation running. Um in our case, we set it to be 210 seconds

takeaways.technique: Seed guidance as a curated markdown context file
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of ad-hoc prompting, they point the agent at a markdown file containing accumulated domain knowledge, known-good ideas, and hard constraints, giving the search its best starting prior.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can simply point it to a markdown file, have all of your information and context in there

takeaways.what_they_do: Operators can open any node, read the exact diff behind a score, and inject a plain-English idea that opens a new branch with its own compute budget while the loop keeps running.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I can also put a budget to each node so it spends compute where I want
takeaways.numbers: Agent plateaued 5 days, then fused a human-shipped tokenizer within 8 hours for the biggest jump in weeks

takeaways.what_they_do: When multiple objectives exist, they collapse to one scalar by weighting or by holding some metrics as hard constraints and optimizing one (e.g. hold model size, optimize accuracy).
takeaways.evidence_quote: you treat some of the matrix as constraint and optimize for one of them
